answer.question: Why were aducanumab's ENGAGE and EMERGE trials stopped for futility, and what did the fuller data show?

claims.claim: Both phase III studies ENGAGE and EMERGE stopped after an interim futility analysis.
claims.repaired_from: ENGAGE and EMERGE were phase III trials of aducanumab; both were stopped after an interim futility analysis.

evidence.subject: P05
evidence.source_record: section 'How analysis after failure changed development' row 5

claims.claim: The prespecified primary endpoint for both trials was change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78.
In ENGAGE, neither aducanumab dose separated from placebo on CDR-SB: low dose difference 0.11 (95% CI -0.469 to 0.403, p=0.225); high dose difference 0.03 (95% CI -0.262 to 0.326, p=0.833).

In EMERGE, the high-dose group showed a statistically significant CDR-SB benefit versus placebo (-0.39, 95% CI -0.694 to -0.086, p=0.012), while the low-dose group did not (-0.26, 95% CI -0.569 to 0.041, p=0.0901).
A larger data cut made EMERGE positive; exposure-related analyses were offered to explain discordant ENGAGE results.

claims.claim: In EMERGE, the primary CDR-SB change at Week 78 showed a difference vs placebo of -0.26 (p=0.0901) for one dose and -0.39 (p=0.012) for the higher dose, indicating a nominally significant benefit only at the higher dose.

EMERGE secondary ADAS-Cog 13 results were -0.701 (p=0.1962) for one dose and -1.4 (p=0.0097) vs placebo, while ENGAGE ADAS-Cog 13 results were -0.583 (p=0.2536) and -0.588 (p=0.2578), neither significant.
EMERGE secondary ADCS-ADL-MCI results were 0.7 (p=0.1515) and 1.7 (p=0.0006) vs placebo, while ENGAGE ADCS-ADL-MCI results were 0.7 (p=0.1225) and 0.7 (p=0.1506), neither significant.
EMERGE secondary MMSE results were -0.1 (p=0.7578) and 0.6 (p=0.0493) vs placebo, while ENGAGE MMSE results were 0.2 (p=0.4795) and -0.1 (p=0.8106), neither consistently significant.

After the futility stop, Biogen reversed the abandonment decision and submitted for approval; a larger data cut made EMERGE positive, and exposure-related analyses were offered to explain discordant ENGAGE results.
